knowledge_point.title: Expressing Flux Over a Surface as a Repeated Integral

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vector field $\mathbf F(x,y,z)=⟨2 x - y,\,x + y,\,2 - 2 z⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined by $z=2 x^{2} + y^{2}$ for $1\le x\le 5$ and $-2\le y\le 5$. Orient $S$ so that its normal has a positive $\mathbf k$-component.

Using the parametrization $x=u$ and $y=v$, the flux through $S$ can be expressed as

$$
\iint_S\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf S={\int }_{1}^{5}{\int }_{-2}^{5}\boxed{\phantom{AAAAAAA}}\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.
$$

What is the missing expression?
question.:question/worked-solution:
The parametrization and its parameter domain are

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,2 u^{2} + v^{2}⟩
$$



$$
D=\{(u,v):1\le u\le 5,\ -2\le v\le 5\}.
$$

Differentiate and compute the natural vector area element:

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf r_u&=⟨1,\,0,\,4 u⟩ \\ \mathbf r_v&=⟨0,\,1,\,2 v⟩ \\ \mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v&=\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf i & \mathbf j & \mathbf k \\ 1 & 0 & 4 u \\ 0 & 1 & 2 v\end{vmatrix} \\ &=⟨- 4 u,\,- 2 v,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

The cross product already has the requested orientation, so

$$
\mathbf N=\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v=⟨- 4 u,\,- 2 v,\,1⟩.
$$

Write $\mathbf F=\langle P,Q,R\rangle$. Substitute all three coordinates into each component:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\mathbf r(u,v))&=2 (u) - (v) \\ &=2 u - v.\end{aligned}
$$



$$
\begin{aligned}Q(\mathbf r(u,v))&=(u) + (v) \\ &=u + v.\end{aligned}
$$



$$
\begin{aligned}R(\mathbf r(u,v))&=2 - 2 (2 u^{2} + v^{2}) \\ &=- 4 u^{2} - 2 v^{2} + 2.\end{aligned}
$$

Form the oriented dot product and collect like terms:

$$
I(u,v)=\mathbf F(\mathbf r(u,v))\cdot\mathbf N.
$$

Its three contributions are

$$
\begin{aligned}T_1&=(2 u - v)(- 4 u) \\ &=- 8 u^{2} + 4 uv.\end{aligned}
$$



$$
\begin{aligned}T_2&=(u + v)(- 2 v) \\ &=- 2 uv - 2 v^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$



$$
\begin{aligned}T_3&=(- 4 u^{2} - 2 v^{2} + 2)(1) \\ &=- 4 u^{2} - 2 v^{2} + 2.\end{aligned}
$$

Adding them gives the missing integrand:

$$
\begin{aligned}I(u,v)&=T_1+T_2+T_3 \\ &=- 12 u^{2} + 2 uv - 4 v^{2} + 2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\iint_S\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf S={\int }_{1}^{5}{\int }_{-2}^{5}I(u,v)\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.
$$

The missing expression is $- 12 u^{2} + 2 uv - 4 v^{2} + 2$.

knowledge_point.title: Expressing Flux Over a Surface as a Repeated Integral

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vector field $\mathbf F(x,y,z)=⟨2 x + y,\,- 2 x + y,\,z - 2⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined by $z=- x^{2} - y^{2}$ for $1\le x\le 3$ and $-2\le y\le 4$. Orient $S$ so that its normal has a positive $\mathbf k$-component.

Using the parametrization $x=u$ and $y=v$, the flux through $S$ can be expressed as

$$
\iint_S\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf S={\int }_{1}^{3}{\int }_{-2}^{4}\boxed{\phantom{AAAAAAA}}\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.
$$

What is the missing expression?
question.:question/worked-solution:
The parametrization and its parameter domain are

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,- u^{2} - v^{2}⟩
$$



$$
D=\{(u,v):1\le u\le 3,\ -2\le v\le 4\}.
$$

Differentiate and compute the natural vector area element:

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf r_u&=⟨1,\,0,\,- 2 u⟩ \\ \mathbf r_v&=⟨0,\,1,\,- 2 v⟩ \\ \mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v&=\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf i & \mathbf j & \mathbf k \\ 1 & 0 & - 2 u \\ 0 & 1 & - 2 v\end{vmatrix} \\ &=⟨2 u,\,2 v,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

The cross product already has the requested orientation, so

$$
\mathbf N=\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v=⟨2 u,\,2 v,\,1⟩.
$$

Write $\mathbf F=\langle P,Q,R\rangle$. Substitute all three coordinates into each component:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\mathbf r(u,v))&=2 (u) + (v) \\ &=2 u + v.\end{aligned}
$$



$$
\begin{aligned}Q(\mathbf r(u,v))&=- 2 (u) + (v) \\ &=- 2 u + v.\end{aligned}
$$



$$
\begin{aligned}R(\mathbf r(u,v))&=(- u^{2} - v^{2}) - 2 \\ &=- u^{2} - v^{2} - 2.\end{aligned}
$$

Form the oriented dot product and collect like terms:

$$
I(u,v)=\mathbf F(\mathbf r(u,v))\cdot\mathbf N.
$$

Its three contributions are

$$
\begin{aligned}T_1&=(2 u + v)(2 u) \\ &=4 u^{2} + 2 uv.\end{aligned}
$$



$$
\begin{aligned}T_2&=(- 2 u + v)(2 v) \\ &=- 4 uv + 2 v^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$



$$
\begin{aligned}T_3&=(- u^{2} - v^{2} - 2)(1) \\ &=- u^{2} - v^{2} - 2.\end{aligned}
$$

Adding them gives the missing integrand:

$$
\begin{aligned}I(u,v)&=T_1+T_2+T_3 \\ &=3 u^{2} - 2 uv + v^{2} - 2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\iint_S\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf S={\int }_{1}^{3}{\int }_{-2}^{4}I(u,v)\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.
$$

The missing expression is $3 u^{2} - 2 uv + v^{2} - 2$.

knowledge_point.title: Expressing Flux Over a Surface as a Repeated Integral

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vector field $\mathbf F(x,y,z)=⟨3 x + 2 y,\,- x + 2 y,\,- z - 2⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined by $z=- 2 x^{2} + 2 y^{2}$ for $-1\le x\le 2$ and $-1\le y\le 3$. Orient $S$ so that its normal has a positive $\mathbf k$-component.

Using the parametrization $x=u$ and $y=v$, the flux through $S$ can be expressed as

$$
\iint_S\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf S={\int }_{-1}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{3}\boxed{\phantom{AAAAAAA}}\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.
$$

What is the missing expression?
question.:question/worked-solution:
The parametrization and its parameter domain are

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,- 2 u^{2} + 2 v^{2}⟩
$$



$$
D=\{(u,v):-1\le u\le 2,\ -1\le v\le 3\}.
$$

Differentiate and compute the natural vector area element:

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf r_u&=⟨1,\,0,\,- 4 u⟩ \\ \mathbf r_v&=⟨0,\,1,\,4 v⟩ \\ \mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v&=\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf i & \mathbf j & \mathbf k \\ 1 & 0 & - 4 u \\ 0 & 1 & 4 v\end{vmatrix} \\ &=⟨4 u,\,- 4 v,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

The cross product already has the requested orientation, so

$$
\mathbf N=\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v=⟨4 u,\,- 4 v,\,1⟩.
$$

Write $\mathbf F=\langle P,Q,R\rangle$. Substitute all three coordinates into each component:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\mathbf r(u,v))&=3 (u) + 2 (v) \\ &=3 u + 2 v.\end{aligned}
$$



$$
\begin{aligned}Q(\mathbf r(u,v))&=- (u) + 2 (v) \\ &=- u + 2 v.\end{aligned}
$$



$$
\begin{aligned}R(\mathbf r(u,v))&=- (- 2 u^{2} + 2 v^{2}) - 2 \\ &=2 u^{2} - 2 v^{2} - 2.\end{aligned}
$$

Form the oriented dot product and collect like terms:

$$
I(u,v)=\mathbf F(\mathbf r(u,v))\cdot\mathbf N.
$$

Its three contributions are

$$
\begin{aligned}T_1&=(3 u + 2 v)(4 u) \\ &=12 u^{2} + 8 uv.\end{aligned}
$$



$$
\begin{aligned}T_2&=(- u + 2 v)(- 4 v) \\ &=4 uv - 8 v^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$



$$
\begin{aligned}T_3&=(2 u^{2} - 2 v^{2} - 2)(1) \\ &=2 u^{2} - 2 v^{2} - 2.\end{aligned}
$$

Adding them gives the missing integrand:

$$
\begin{aligned}I(u,v)&=T_1+T_2+T_3 \\ &=14 u^{2} + 12 uv - 10 v^{2} - 2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\iint_S\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf S={\int }_{-1}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{3}I(u,v)\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.
$$

The missing expression is $14 u^{2} + 12 uv - 10 v^{2} - 2$.
